content:
Aisha: Quick sync request: we've had a support ticket where a customers long-running ETL job got throttled after we flipped cache TTLs. They were using an org key without derivation. Need to decide how long-running workers should authenticate w/o weakening security.
Tom: Oof. We pushed derived-token TTLs down to 1m for hot routes to protect skimming attacks. But batch jobs respawn lots of connections, they need a stable path.
Priya: Two options: 1) let jobs exchange for a "bound" long-lived derived token (host-bound, limited scope), or 2) provide a server-side client credential flow where the job daemon asks our control plane for ephemeral creds tied to an instance id.
Nate: I prefer host-bound derived tokens. Simpler: exchange endpoint accepts a signed host assertion (HMAC using a pre-registered machine key) and returns a derived token with longer TTL and extra constraint claim (hwf=host:abc123).
Aisha: That requires job registration. Ops concerns: how do we onboard those machine keys securely? For Dedicated/private we could accept a PKCS#11 attestation. For hosted customers we can do a web UI to register a fingerprint and set admin approval.
Tom: Implementation note: derived token should include a 'cnf' claim for confirmation methods (e.g., cnf.hmac_key_id) so runtime verifies binding on each request. Verification should be cheap: HMAC of request+nonce checked at edge before considering token valid.
Priya: Agree on cnf pattern. Also we should avoid adding heavy crypto to the hot path for normal (short-lived) derived tokens. Host-bound flows only for long-lived exchanges. Normal flow remains: API key -> exchange -> short derived token (no extra binding).
Nate: Edge caching: some runtime nodes live in regional edge pods where we want zero DB hops. Derived tokens should be self-contained (signed) and verifiable by edge using public key set. We'll publish our signing keyset with rotation metadata to S3/CDN and rotate keys with version ids (kid).
Aisha: That helps Dedicated too, but private deployments may not want our CDN. For Private, the customer control-plane will sign derived tokens locally using their KMS; runtimes will trust local keyset. Need config flag to disable fetching external keyset.
Tom: Revocation model for self-contained tokens: maintain a small revocation bloom per-region pushed to edges via pubsub. Because long-lived bound tokens are rarer, the bloom stays small. For short tokens TTL is primary revocation mechanism.
Priya: We should track "issued_for" metadata so we can query: which canonical key resulted in how many long-lived derivations. Console needs a filter for long-lived tokens per key.
Nate: Another gotcha: cross-project delegation. If a service has permissions across projects, derived token must carry explicit allowed projects list, not a wildcard. We should cap array size and reject tokens that exceed configured limit.
Aisha: UX: console checkbox per key: "Allow long-lived job tokens (requires admin approval)". Default off for org keys, on for project keys. Also a bulk migrate flow to toggle for existing project keys.
Tom: Security review: require multi-admin approval for enabling long-lived on an org key. Also make sure issuance events create a Git-style auditable record (who approved, when, justification).
Priya: Runtime acceptance logic pseudo: 1) if token is canonical api key -> do canonical lookup and optionally issue derived; 2) if token is derived -> verify sig and exp, check revocation bloom/jti list, if cnf present validate binding; 3) enforce route-level scope. Keep checks in that order for perf.
Nate: For implementation we can add a lightweight middleware in edge runtime written in Rust that verifies derived tokens and only queries Redis for revocation hits. Hot-path avoids DB.
Aisha: Ops-bot: filing GH issue #4210 for middleware spike and #4211 for console wireframes.
Tom: One small detail: signing key rotation. We need to accept tokens signed by previous keys for a short grace window, and publish key rotation events so edges can fetch new keys. Also plan key rollover tests in chaos env.
Priya: Also rate-limit exchanges per canonical key and per origin IP to prevent mass minting. Add a quota in control plane with soft/ hard limits.
Nate: Thoughts on backwards compatibility: don't change token header for now. Use new claim names under short keys (cnf, issued_for) to avoid breaking older runtimes. Runtime version gate: only newer runtimes enforce cnf.
Aisha: OK summary: - Short-lived derived tokens remain default for interactive/high-volume routes. - Long-lived host-bound derived tokens supported via admin-approved exchange with cnf claim and host HMAC. - Self-contained signing + pubsub-bloom revocation for edges. - Console/UX flags and audit trails. - Work items: edge middleware spike (Nate/Tom), console approval UX (Priya), migration playbook (Aisha).
ops-bot: Assigned: #4210 to @nate,@tom; #4211 to @priya; #4212 to @aisha.
Aisha: If nobody objects I'll start drafting migration playbook and a short security checklist.
Tom: No objections. One ask: include a recovery/incident play for compromised long-lived tokens.
Priya: Agreed. Add forced rotation + global revoke endpoint + customer notif flow.
Nate: I'll start the middleware spike tomorrow.
Aisha: Perfect. Closing for now, will post the draft in this thread. :white_check_mark:
